note: Push names: all four push readings stay as built. P-1 plain words name gates (AT-AP-04 R3-02); P-2 a push approval that names no branch is protected-push, whatever branch is checked out; P-3 a local merge naming a protected branch is protected-push; P-4 a name after a remote prefix counts as that branch (team/release is release); the remote default branch (origin/dev) and a protected name (release) are gates. A named push of feat/x, a local merge into feat/x and team/feat-y carry, so the case is not one that asks for everything. Summary path (measure --compact --copy); the row counts the carried approvals by origin. What names a branch for P-2 (review of the first build: any word with a slash used to count): a `branch <name>` target, a refspec of a git push (either side of src:dst) or a branch-shaped name right after "push" in plain words. A file-path target (U-10), a repo slug (U-11) and `git push origin HEAD` (U-12) name none and ask; plain "push feat/z" (U-13) and `HEAD:feat/q` (U-14) name one and carry. Second review (each gate here carried on 8b498a2): a name counts only with a letter and either a slash or a branch that exists in the repository, so "push the follow-up fix" (U-15), "push 2 commits" (U-16), "push the 2 commits" (U-23), `git push origin qa` with no qa branch (U-24), "push this branch to origin" (U-19) and "push the branch up" (U-20) name none; a `git push` holding `$(...)` or a backtick names none (U-17, U-18, U-28); a tag push names none (`v1.2.0`, U-22; `refs/tags/`, U-27); "to main!" is main (U-21). The existing branch rel-2 (U-25) and fix/tag-parser (U-26) carry.
